candidates.name: Tailwind CSS v4 built-in container queries

evidence.claim: The official repository is active and is the source of the installed Tailwind framework.
Official v4 documentation demonstrates @container with container breakpoint and @max-* variants for grid composition.
The installed 4.3.3 release is MIT-licensed and current in the project lockfile.

risks: An arbitrary container breakpoint could preserve clipping or switch columns too early.
The query container must wrap the width-constrained provider composition rather than an unconstrained ancestor.
candidates.decision_rationale: Native container variants directly match the panel-width requirement, are already installed, and follow an existing repository convention without adding React state or a dependency.

candidates.name: Playwright Test

evidence.claim: The official repository is active and backs the project's installed browser-test framework.
Official documentation supports explicit viewport dimensions for responsive tests.
Playwright Test provides retrying locator assertions and element screenshot assertions.
The project-installed 1.62.1 release is Apache-2.0 licensed.

risks: A narrow viewport alone does not prove response to a constrained provider panel inside a wide viewport.
Screenshot-only evidence can miss semantic keyboard regressions unless paired with functional assertions.
candidates.decision_rationale: The existing runner can prove layout geometry, overflow, and keyboard access in a real browser; no new test framework is needed.

candidates.name: @tailwindcss/container-queries

evidence.claim: The official plugin describes itself as container-query utilities for Tailwind CSS v3.2+.
Tailwind CSS v4 documents the required container variants as built-in framework behavior.
The separate plugin remains available as version 0.1.1 under MIT.

risks: Adds a redundant dependency to a Tailwind v4 project.
Creates ambiguity between legacy plugin guidance and native v4 syntax.
candidates.decision_rationale: The installed Tailwind version already includes the feature, so the plugin provides no needed capability.

candidates.name: use-resize-observer

evidence.claim: The repository is active and provides the published React measurement hook.
Registry metadata describes a React hook that measures element size with ResizeObserver; version 10.0.0 is MIT-licensed.

risks: Introduces resize-driven component state and rerenders for presentation-only layout.
Requires JavaScript before the layout can adapt even though CSS container queries are available.
candidates.decision_rationale: Measurement is technically viable but adds runtime complexity that the existing CSS framework avoids.

candidates.name: Intrinsic CSS Grid auto-fit/minmax pattern

evidence.claim: Official Tailwind documentation demonstrates arbitrary grid-template column values using grid-cols-[repeat(...)], which can express intrinsic CSS grid templates.

risks: A general auto-fit template can create more than two columns at large widths, violating the explicit desktop two-column composition.
Preventing a third column requires an additional maximum width or template constraint, reducing the breakpoint-free advantage.
candidates.decision_rationale: This is a valid no-dependency responsive pattern and should remain a planning reference, but native container variants map more directly to the contract's exact one-column versus two-column states.

build_required.need: Provider-specific container boundary, breakpoint, and grid classes
build_required.why_no_candidate: Tailwind supplies the primitive, but the application must identify the constrained provider ancestor and select a breakpoint that preserves the incumbent field minimums and padding.

build_required.need: Focused browser fixture and assertions for constrained and desktop provider-panel widths
build_required.why_no_candidate: Playwright supplies the runner and APIs, but deterministic provider data, panel constraint setup, layout geometry, overflow, and keyboard assertions are application-specific.

build_required.need: Review packet inclusion check for goals, progress, source excerpts, and focused evidence
build_required.why_no_candidate: This is a local KBD artifact-construction requirement inherited from the assessment judge, not a missing external library.
